# 1.2.64 - secrets out of the world's data

The eighth stage on the way to 1.3.0. Foundry sends every world setting, and
every actor's, user's, token's, item's and chat card's data, to every browser,
where a console reads it whatever the screen shows. 1.2.64 takes what only the
GMs, or only one player, may know out of that data and into the GMs' store
1.2.63 introduced: the traps, the dark of an Eclipse, the Key Remnant plan, the
pre-session notes, how an incident happened, a death nobody has found yet, the
Despair counters, what a trace's token and a bullet's flags said, and what was
taken off a body. The world is migrated on the first load, and nothing leaves
the world's data before the store has read it back.

## Before installing

1. **Copy the world** (Foundry's backup of the world in Setup, or a copy of the
   world's folder), as before 1.2.63.
2. **After the first load as the primary GM, Back up the case** (GM panel,
   Between sessions). The file now holds more of the case than it did on 1.2.63;
   keep it where no player can open it.

## The migration

A moment after the first load of 1.2.64, the primary GM's browser moves into
the GMs' store: each trap's killer, builders, condition and trigger, and a
project's saboteur; the Direct Murders declared in a running Eclipse and its
crossings; the Key Remnant plan; the pre-session notes' text; a running
incident's method (a trap, self-inflicted, how it ended); the overflow's count;
what was taken off each body; and which trace each Truth Bullet came from. It
puts the neutral name and picture back on traces' tokens that earlier builds
had named, moves the answer keys still left on old traces' tokens into the case,
takes the incident mark off old incidents' traces, and drops the Reroll
bookmarks and the Search cards' facts from the world's data. A world stamped
1.2.63 runs the Faint Prep pass again.

A step that cannot read back what it moved leaves the world as it was and a
notice that stays on screen ("the data migration stopped short"), and the next
load of the world tries again.

## Do not go back to 1.2.63

A 1.2.63 build reads the world data 1.2.64 emptied, and loses: each trap's
killer, builders, condition and trigger (armed or fired) and a project's
saboteur; the Direct Murders declared in a running Eclipse and its crossings;
the Key Remnant plan; the pre-session notes' text; a running incident's method;
the overflow's count; what was taken off each body; and which trace each Truth
Bullet came from, so players stop seeing the traces they found. Never in
1.2.63's world data at all, so also gone: a death kept until its body is found
(the victim reads alive), a Reinforced Level Up waiting for the class, and the
Despair owed for conversions. Dropped on the update either way: the Reroll
bookmarks (a Reroll right after the update finds nothing to replay) and the
Search cards' facts for a day summary that spans the update.

## Changed

- **A trap is the GMs'**: who built it, who the killer is, what sets it off and
  whether it is armed or fired, and who sabotaged a project, are no longer in
  the world's data.
- **The dark of an Eclipse is the GMs'**: a Direct Murder declared in it is kept
  by the GMs from the declaration to the lights, and a declaration outside a
  running Eclipse is refused. The crossings are counted and judged by the
  primary GM's browser, and the crossing's card goes privately to the mover
  alone, naming the room crossed into.
- **The Key Remnant plan is kept by the GMs, a chapter at a time**; a season
  reset keeps one chapter's plan.
- **A pre-session note's words are the GMs' and its writer's alone.** A note
  saved while no GM is online waits on its writer's browser until one connects,
  and a player's Save keeps a GM's newer edit.
- **A death kept until the body is found.** When the running incident's victim
  dies (or **A character dies** is used with *Keep it the GMs' until the body is
  found* ticked), nothing reaches the table: no deceased flag, no dead marker,
  and the Truth Bullets stay on the sheet. The death card and its sound go to
  the GMs and the incident's players; the victim's own player and, later, a
  lone finder know of it too. The discovery publishes it.
- **The trial asks only for the killers of deaths the table knows.** A victim
  nobody has found gets a ballot, and levels up with the class at a right
  verdict.
- **A surviving Blackened's Reinforced Level Up waits for the class**: after a
  wrong verdict its owner is told on a veiled card, and the class's next correct
  verdict opens one window per survivor, the Standard and the Reinforced picked
  together (1 + 3). What is still waiting at the Final Trial's verdict is given
  there.
- **The Despair counters are the GMs'**: the overflow's count is kept by the
  GMs, and a conversion of Despair to Hope gives the Hope at once while the
  pool's drop is owed and paid at the next time of day. The GM panel shows what
  the pool owes, and only the pool less what it owes can be spent.
- **A trace's token keeps its neutral name and "?" picture on every screen.**
  A GM's screen draws the rest from the case, and a finder's from their own
  Truth Bullet. A Truth Bullet no longer names its trace in its flags.
- **What was taken off a body is the GMs'.** A loot before the discovery gives
  its Truth Bullet at the publication, and names no body before then. An
  incident's traces are no longer drawn for the cast of a later incident.
- **A Reroll's bookmark stays in the roller's browser**, and a Search card's
  facts travel with its words, not in its flags.
- **How an incident happened is the cast's**: whether by a trap, by the victim's
  own hand, and how it ended.
- **Small screens that told too much**: the HUD's explainer shows the clock the
  HUD shows; a redacted sheet no longer carries its action tooltips or the Calls
  armed on the owner's next roll. The advice to set the Mastermind to "- nobody
  -" is gone, and the season checklist and the case health check say when it
  has been followed anyway.
- **Regional voice**: a victim leaves the room's voice at the kill, not at the
  discovery. The season checklist and the voice diagnostics warn when a
  self-hosted LiveKit server's secret is stored in the world.

## Known gaps

- Daggerheart's Countdowns (a secret project's name, progress and viewers) stay
  world data in 1.2.64.
- A self-hosted LiveKit server's API secret is another module's world setting:
  the module warns about it and does not move it.
- Where every token stands, every actor's data (a victim's Health at 0
  included) and every item's move stay world data (GM handbook, section 1).
- A loot before the discovery still moves the item and places the loot trace,
  hidden, at the body.
- A body's first loot's Truth Bullet keeps "taken from a body" in its name
  instead of the trace's neutral name.
- A death kept from an earlier chapter is not found automatically, and no later
  trial asks for its killer; the trial's start tells the GM.
- A Blackened who is themselves a death nobody has found is not executed at a
  right verdict; the GM publishes that death by hand.
- A lone finder may be a killer of the chapter's other incident.
- A Reroll of a roll made in another browser has nothing to replay.
- A draft note kept while no GM was online goes as written when one connects.
- A trace kept on its token by the migration keeps its flags until the GM sets
  its promotion; there is no in-module way to drop them.
- An old trace placed within ten minutes before a running incident opened keeps
  its incident mark until that incident closes.
- Two GMs writing the same row in the same moment (a loot served while another
  GM publishes that death, a conversion as the time of day moves): the later
  write wins. Read in the code, not measured at a table.
- A hand-set "dead" status without the module's record does not stop a trap:
  a death is the module's record.

## Checked

- The headless suite: 434 passed, 0 failed, 17 skipped, 0 red until a later
  stage. New in the suite: R190 to R200. Scenario 72-canary walks a chapter (a
  trap, an Eclipse, an incident, a death nobody has found, the discovery, the
  verdict) and scans the world's data after each step; five known leaks close
  with this release (S01-01, S02-11, S09-05, S10-01, S11-03). One test more is
  skipped: a found trace's token is drawn on a canvas, which the harness does
  not have. Scenario 14's intermittent failure is fixed: the room fog's
  stand-down wrote the page's class list even when it had nothing to change. The
  scenarios end green: 61-gmstore-case 83/83, the security scenario 88/88, and
  72-canary 66/69, its three expected reds each a later stage's or a Foundry
  limit, as 11-killer-secrecy's one is E06's.
- An independent review in two rounds (security, and whether the change is
  correct and its tests measure) listed four larger problems and forty-one
  smaller ones, some of them the same finding seen by both reviewers. Each is
  fixed here or listed above as a known gap. The larger ones: a migration step
  that could not read back its rows marked the world migrated anyway; the trial
  counted the killer of a death nobody had found; and a loot before the
  discovery named the body on the taker's Truth Bullet.
- Not checked in a real Foundry yet, and listed in the audit's live checks
  (LIVE-E05-01 to 14): a player's console through a whole chapter, the
  migration on a copy of a played world, the dead marker at the publication and
  a lone finder's marker, the victim's voice at the kill, a found trace's drawn
  name and picture, the crossing card, the owed Despair on every HUD, a correct
  verdict after a wrong one, `replaceFlag` and `forcedDeletion()` on v14, a note
  saved with no GM online, the LiveKit warning against the real setting, a
  deletion on a token's own actor data, a drag through two rooms, and the
  taker's drawing of a loot trace. The local release gate needs a local Foundry
  v14 and did not run for this release.
